statement: The central operation registry has watermark operations but no adjudicated partially ordered frontier/capability algebra.
Iteration epoch, feedback delay, fixed-point test and productive-cycle operations are not explicit central operation identities.
No universal channel offer contract yet composes ordering, capacity, acknowledgement, backpressure and barrier behavior.
A machine-checkable end-to-end guarantee proof calculus remains candidate and must distinguish processing from observable effects.
Snapshot/change handoff laws require adjudication across relational logs, document databases, APIs and object manifests.
A universal materialization identity must compose table snapshots, files/manifests, indexes, API destinations and message ranges without collapsing them.
Dynamic task expansion and truly dynamic graph mutation need separate boundedness and replay semantics.
Pushdown compatibility requires exact remote null, collation, time, numeric and error semantics, not operator-name equality.
Atomic publication across heterogeneous sinks is not generally available and must lower to transactions, idempotency plus reconciliation, or compensation.
Portable state schema and migration contracts across independent stream engines are not standardized.
Correct backfill in pipelines with downstream incremental state needs dependency-aware cut and publication planning.
Compression is currently only a decision placeholder; codecs need offers for ratio, CPU, memory, seekability, splittability, dictionaries and corruption behavior.
Receipt signing, key authority, redaction and long-term verification profiles are not yet bound.
Every core semantic and runtime contract still needs conformance against two independent implementations.
